title: Efficiently Scaling Transformer Inference
technique: Analytical model to choose 1D/2D weight-stationary and weight-gathered partitioning for TPU v4 slices, multiquery attention sharding by batch, int8 weights, low-level comm/compute overlap

optimized_metrics.evidence: to achieve a new Pareto frontier on the latency and model FLOPS utilization (MFU) tradeoffs on 500B+ parameter models
a new Pareto frontier on the latency and model FLOPS utilization (MFU) tradeoffs ... a 76% MFU during large-batch-size processing of input tokens
offline inference for scoring or distillation, emphasize high throughput and low cost per token at any latency

Second, we apply memory optimizations and take full advantage of PaLM's multiquery attention to reduce unnecessary tensor overheads and maximize the batch size that fits on a given number of chips, enabling higher throughput.

headline_claim.text: we achieve a low-batch-size latency of 29ms per token during generation (using int8 weight quantization) and a 76% MFU during large-batch-size processing of input tokens, while supporting a long 2048-token context length on the PaLM 540B parameter model.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 1 left, Tables 2-3 (decode latency per generated token)
Fig 1 right (prefill latency per forward pass), Tables 2-3 total inference time (e.g. 1.9 s chatbot)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The latency is the total time for an inference and can be broken down into the time to process the input tokens present at the start of the inference (which we call "prefill") and the time to autoregressively generate output tokens (which we term "decode"). The decode latency can also be measured "per step", i.e. divided by the number of tokens in each sequence.
metric_definitions.notes: Batch-level latency of a statically batched inference; no queueing. Per-step decode latency = TPOT-like

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The throughput of prefill or decode is the number of tokens processed or generated per second.

The model FLOPS utilization (MFU) is the ratio of the observed throughput to the theoretical maximum throughput if the benchmarked hardware setup were operating at peak FLOPS with no memory or communication overhead.
metric_definitions.notes: Defined relative to peak FLOPs; also used as cost proxy (chip-seconds per token)

load_regime: fixed batch size and chip-count sweep tracing the Pareto frontier; context length 2048; no arrival process
tradeoff_acknowledged: Explicit latency vs cost/MFU trade-off: 'Lower latency can often be achieved by using more chips, but this can also result in worse MFU, resulting in a higher total cost (in terms of chip-seconds or dollars) per token.'
workloads: fixed 2048 context; 64 generated tokens; no request traces
extractor_notes: Not a serving system: static-batch offline analysis of latency/cost Pareto. The paper's multi-objective framing (latency vs MFU/cost-per-token at chosen batch size) is the key metric statement. 'Latency target' is a design parameter, not a formal SLO.
